patients.summary: Teacher with Crohn disease, SLE, mild asthma and iron deficiency anemia who joins in 2019; HHT is named in 2021, a Crohn rectovaginal fistula in 2023 and neuropsychiatric lupus with a seizure in late 2023. Post-abortal choriocarcinoma is treated to remission in 2024; after a 2025 cesarean delivery it returns in July 2026 with brain and lung metastases and she is on chemotherapy at today.

documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Caller: Wendy Hastings, DOB 09/05/1989. Wants to transfer primary care here; has been with another practice for years and says the hard part has been getting anyone on the phone between visits. Has Crohn's and lupus, sees GI and rheumatology outside and plans to keep them. Membership terms reviewed, packet emailed. Records release signed electronically for her prior primary care office. New patient visit booked for 9/17 at 8:40, asked to bring all pill bottles and her inhaler.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

30F elementary school teacher transferring care. Main reason for switching: wants a doctor who answers between visits; her specialists are outside and she would like one person keeping the whole list straight.

Crohn's: diagnosed in 2014 at 24 after months of diarrhea and weight loss. Followed by an outside GI group. On mesalamine 1.2 g TID. Says she is quiet right now, 1-2 formed stools a day, no blood.
SLE: diagnosed some years ago by rheumatology (joint pain and a rash at the time per her account, she does not remember the details). Hydroxychloroquine 200 daily and prednisone 10 daily for a long time; GI and rheum have both bumped prednisone up for flares and brought it back down. Has never been off it for long.
Asthma: albuterol maybe once a month, more with colds. No ED visits for asthma, no oral steroid bursts just for asthma.
Nosebleeds: since she was a kid. Comes and goes, a few a month lately, usually stops with pressure. On iron for low blood count for years, assumed from the nosebleeds. No black stools.

PMH as above. PSH: none. Meds reconciled with bottles (5). NKDA.
FH: mother with lupus. Maternal aunt with rheumatoid arthritis. Father gets frequent nosebleeds, as does a cousin on his side.
SH: lives with partner. Never smoker, alcohol 1-2 drinks a month, no drugs. Teaches 2nd grade.
GYN: periods regular. Last Pap 2016 normal.

ROS: no fevers, no joint swelling now, no rash now, no chest pain, no dyspnea at rest. Fatigue at the end of school days, chronic.

EXAM: vitals as charted. Well appearing. HEENT: anterior nares without active bleeding, oropharynx clear. Neck supple, no nodes. Heart RRR, no murmur. Lungs clear, no wheeze. Abdomen soft, nontender, normal bowel sounds. Joints without synovitis. Skin: no malar rash or discoid lesions today. Neuro grossly normal. Pelvic: normal external genitalia, cervix normal appearing, Pap with HPV collected.

A/P
1. Crohn's disease - quiet on mesalamine, GI outside. Will request their notes.
2. SLE on HCQ + chronic prednisone 10 - rheum outside. Needs yearly retinal screening for HCQ; she thinks her last eye exam was last winter. Long-term prednisone: will look at bone density.
3. Mild intermittent asthma - albuterol PRN, adequate.
4. Iron deficiency anemia, likely from chronic nosebleeds - CBC and iron studies today, continue ferrous sulfate.
5. Health maintenance: Pap/HPV today. HIV and hep C screening today. Lipids, A1c (steroid exposure), TSH. Flu shot when the supply arrives next month.

Return in about 4 months, sooner by text.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Wendy, your labs are back. Hemoglobin is a little low at the level your old office was seeing, and your iron stores are on the low side of normal, so keep taking the iron every day. Kidney and liver tests, cholesterol, sugar and thyroid are all normal. HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. Urine was clean. Pap is still pending; I'll message when it's in. Nothing needs changing for now.

documents.title: RE: Your lab results
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you! Nice to get this so fast. Will keep up the iron.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came after school for flu vaccine. No fever today, no prior reaction to flu vaccines. Quadrivalent inactivated 0.5 mL IM left deltoid. VIS reviewed. Tolerated, left after 15 min observation. Pap result (normal, HPV neg) reviewed with her at her request.

Dear colleague, thank you for letting us know Ms. Hastings has joined your practice. We saw her in routine follow-up for systemic lupus erythematosus. She reports no new rash, no joint swelling, no pleuritic pain. Exam today without synovitis or mucocutaneous lesions. Recent labs reviewed. Disease quiet. Plan: continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily and prednisone 10 mg daily; annual retinal screening for hydroxychloroquine (she reports one last winter). Return in 6 months.

Medications: mesalamine 1.2 g TID, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol PRN, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Is prednisone making me high risk?
documents.author: patient
documents.body: School is remote for now. Should I be doing anything different because of the prednisone and lupus? Should I stop the prednisone? I have about 2 weeks left of everything.

documents.title: RE: Is prednisone making me high risk?
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Please don't stop the prednisone on your own - after this many years your body depends on it and stopping suddenly is dangerous. Same for the hydroxychloroquine and mesalamine. Being on prednisone does put you in the group that should be extra careful: stay home as much as you can, masks and hand washing, and let me know right away with fever or cough. I've sent 90-day refills of everything so you have a cushion. Let's do a video check-in in June instead of an office visit.

orders.reason: Recurrent epistaxis with blood-streaked sputum; family history of nosebleeds

documents.title: Office Visit - Epistaxis
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Nosebleeds are now several times a week, worse over the past year. Twice this summer she went to urgent care because pressure did not stop it after 30+ minutes; both times it settled there without packing being left in. Humidifier and saline gel have not changed much. New: every so often she coughs up a little blood-streaked spit in the morning. No actual cough, no shortness of breath, no chest pain. No fever. Her dad has had nosebleeds all his life, and a cousin on his side too.
O: vitals as charted. Afebrile. Nares: dried blood left anterior septum, no active bleeding. Oropharynx clear. Lungs clear to auscultation. Heart RRR.
A/P:
1. Recurrent epistaxis, increasing, with family history on father's side and occasional blood-streaked sputum. I want this looked at with an eye to an inherited vascular cause and the lungs. Referral to pulmonology placed; she'd like the group closest to school. CBC today.
2. Iron deficiency anemia - continue iron.
3. Flu vaccine today.
Return after pulmonology.

documents.title: Blood count and referral
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Wendy, your blood count is about where it has been, no worse. The pulmonology office has the referral; their first opening is December 27. We put you on their cancellation list.

documents.title: Immunization
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pfizer booster 0.3 mL IM right deltoid. Eligible given immunosuppression. Observed 15 minutes, no reaction. Asked when pulmonology is - still 12/27, no cancellation spot yet.

conditions.label: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia
conditions.note: Clinical diagnosis at pulmonology: recurrent epistaxis, mucosal telangiectasias, affected first-degree relative

documents.title: Pulmonology consultation
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Outside pulmonology group - new consultation, date of service 12/27/2021. Faxed 01/20/2022.

Reason for referral: recurrent epistaxis, occasional blood-tinged sputum.

History: 32-year-old woman with Crohn's disease, SLE and mild intermittent asthma. Nosebleeds since childhood; over the last year they have become much more frequent, several per week, and on occasion she has needed medical care to stop them. She has noticed occasional blood in her sputum. She denies cough and dyspnea. Her father and a paternal cousin have the same problem.

Medications: mesalamine 1.2 g TID, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol 90 mcg 2 puffs q4-6h PRN, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily. NKDA. Never smoker.

Exam: comfortable, SpO2 normal on room air. Several small red to violaceous telangiectasias on the lips and buccal mucosa. Chest clear bilaterally, no bruits over the lung fields. No clubbing or cyanosis.

Data: hemoglobin 11.2 g/dL, platelets 250 K/uL, INR 1.0, PTT 30 s.

Assessment: recurrent spontaneous epistaxis, mucocutaneous telangiectasias and a first-degree relative with the same picture meet clinical criteria for hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (Osler-Weber-Rendu). Coagulation is normal. Mild anemia consistent with chronic blood loss.

Plan: transthoracic echocardiogram with agitated saline to screen for pulmonary arteriovenous malformation. Continue oral iron. Nasal moisturization. Genetic counseling information given. We will forward the echo result.

reports.text: Indication: hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, screening for intrapulmonary shunt. Left ventricle normal in size with normal wall thickness and systolic function, estimated LVEF 60-65%. Normal diastolic filling. Right ventricle normal size and function. Atria normal. Valves structurally normal without significant regurgitation. Estimated RVSP normal. No pericardial effusion. Agitated saline contrast injected at rest and with Valsalva maneuver: no bubbles seen in the left heart at any cycle.
reports.conclusion: Normal echocardiogram. Negative agitated-saline study; no evidence of intracardiac or intrapulmonary shunt.

documents.title: Echo reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Bubble echo negative, no lung AVM shunt. Pulm letter arrived last week - HHT diagnosis. Visit already booked 2/8 to go over it.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit - HHT
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here to go over pulmonology. She was relieved there is a name for the nosebleeds. Bubble echo negative. Says her father has since been told by his own doctor that he likely has the same thing. Nosebleeds still several a week. Occasional streaky sputum unchanged. No dyspnea.
O: vitals as charted. Small telangiectasias on the lower lip. Lungs clear.
A/P:
1. Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia, newly diagnosed by pulmonology (clinical criteria). Added to problem list; family history updated (father HHT). Bubble echo negative. Continue nasal moisturization; iron. We'll watch hemoglobin every 6 months.
2. Immunizations: on chronic prednisone and hydroxychloroquine, so she qualifies for pneumococcal and shingles vaccines now. PCV20 and Shingrix #1 today; Shingrix #2 in 2-6 months.
3. SLE/Crohn's: stable per specialists.
RTC 4-6 months.

New class this year, 24 kids, likes them. Mood good, PHQ-9 2. Walking most evenings.

Prevention: Pap 2019 normal, due 2024. Pneumococcal and shingles complete. Flu and bivalent COVID booster today. HCQ eye exam July, normal.

documents.title: Platelet count
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Wendy, one number was off this time: your platelets (the clotting cells) were a bit low at 118, when they are usually normal. That can happen with a recent virus or just lab variation. Any unusual bruising, blood spots on the skin, or nosebleeds worse than your usual? If not, let's simply repeat it in about a month.

documents.title: Office Visit - GI symptoms
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Since about January, on and off crampy lower abdominal pain and loose stools, 3-5 a day on bad days, then a few good days. No blood she has seen. Pants are looser; down about 2.5 kg from her usual. No fever. No travel, no antibiotics, nobody sick at home. Her GI follow-up isn't until late summer.
O: vitals as charted, afebrile. Abdomen soft, mild tenderness in the lower abdomen, no guarding, no mass. Weight down from her baseline.
A/P: Probable Crohn's flare. She is already on prednisone 10 and mesalamine; no change until GI sees her. Called GI office - visit moved up to 6/30, the soonest they have, with instruction to call them sooner if pain worsens or bleeding starts. CBC, CMP today. Hydrate. If fever or severe pain, ED.

results.text: No enteric pathogens isolated. Ova and parasites: none seen.

documents.title: Gastroenterology consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology - visit 06/30/2023 (letter dictated 07/05).

HPI: Ms. Hastings, 33, with Crohn's disease for about nine years on mesalamine and long-term low-dose prednisone, plus SLE and hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia. For roughly six months she has had episodic abdominal pain and diarrhea with weight loss she did not intend. Over the last several weeks she has also had a foul-smelling tan vaginal discharge and has occasionally passed gas through the vagina.

Meds: mesalamine 1.2 g three times daily, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol as needed, ferrous sulfate daily. NKDA.

Exam: afebrile. Weight 73 kg. Abdomen tender in the right lower quadrant, no rebound, no guarding, no mass. Perianal skin intact. Speculum and digital exam with chaperone: a small lesion on the posterior vaginal wall in keeping with a fistula opening.

Labs today: hemoglobin 12.1, WBC 9.0, CRP 24 mg/L (ref <5). Stool culture negative for enteric pathogens; no ova or parasites.

Impression: active Crohn's disease complicated by a rectovaginal fistula.

Plan:
1. MRI pelvis (fistula protocol).
2. Colorectal surgery referral for exam under anesthesia and drainage.
3. Metronidazole 500 mg three times daily for 4 weeks.
4. Prednisone 40 mg daily, decreasing by 5 mg each week back to her 10 mg dose.
5. Continue mesalamine. Follow-up after surgery.

documents.title: Hydroxychloroquine retinal screening
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body: Outside ophthalmology - exam 07/19/2023. Hydroxychloroquine screening, year 4 in our office. Acuity 20/20 OU, normal dilated exam, fields full, OCT normal. No retinopathy. Next in 12 months.

documents.title: Colorectal surgery operative letter
documents.author: colorectal surgery
documents.body:
Outside colorectal surgery - consult 07/27/2023; procedure 08/10/2023.

MRI pelvis 07/18/2023 (fistula protocol): low rectovaginal fistula from the anterior lower rectum to the posterior vaginal wall. No abscess or collection. No other fistula tracks.

Procedure: examination under anesthesia, placement of a loose draining seton through the rectovaginal fistula. Findings: single low tract, no abscess. No complications. Discharged same day.

Post-op plan: sitz baths, keep stools soft; seton to remain long-term while Crohn's therapy is optimized by GI; follow-up in clinic in 6 weeks.

Medications at discharge: unchanged home medications; completing metronidazole course. Allergies: NKDA.

events.reason: ED record and discharge summary received

reports.study: MRI brain without and with contrast
reports.text: Indication: new-onset seizure, SLE. Technique: multiplanar multisequence MRI of the brain before and after IV gadolinium. Findings: no acute infarct on diffusion imaging. No hemorrhage. No mass or abnormal enhancement. Ventricles and sulci normal for age. No white matter lesions. No vascular malformation; normal flow voids. Pituitary and orbits unremarkable.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 12/29/2023, arrival 15:05 by ambulance.

CC: seizure.
HPI: 34-year-old woman with SLE, Crohn's disease and HHT. Per boyfriend, she had a generalized tonic-clonic seizure at home, then was confused. He says that over the past several months she has complained of headaches and fatigue, and a red rash on her face has flared when she is in the sun. No prior seizures. No head trauma.
Meds: mesalamine 1.2 g TID, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol PRN, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily. NKDA.

Vitals: T 37.8 C (100.0 F), BP 135/85, HR 88.
Exam: postictal, rouses to voice and follows commands. Erythematous rash across both malar areas and the nasal bridge. Oral mucosa without ulcers. Neuro: moves all extremities symmetrically, no focal deficit. Tongue without laceration.

Labs: Hgb 11.2, WBC 3.8, platelets 95 K. Creatinine 1.1. UA: protein 2+, RBC 5-10/hpf. ANA positive. Anti-dsDNA positive. C3 low, C4 low.

Assessment: new-onset generalized seizure in active SLE with cytopenias and low complements - concern for neuropsychiatric lupus. Admitted to medicine with neurology and rheumatology consults.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital - Medicine. Admitted 12/29/2023, discharged 01/02/2024.

Principal diagnosis: neuropsychiatric systemic lupus erythematosus presenting with generalized tonic-clonic seizure.
Secondary: SLE with leukopenia, thrombocytopenia and hypocomplementemia; Crohn's disease with rectovaginal fistula (seton); hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia; mild intermittent asthma; anemia.

Course: Neurology and rheumatology consulted. MRI brain with and without contrast normal. Routine EEG: normal background, no epileptiform discharges. No further seizures. Treated with IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 3 days, then prednisone 40 mg daily. Levetiracetam 500 mg twice daily started. Headache resolved. Rash improving.

Discharge medications:
- levetiracetam 500 mg PO BID (NEW)
- prednisone 40 mg PO daily, decrease by 5 mg each week to 10 mg daily (CHANGED)
- hydroxychloroquine 200 mg PO daily
- mesalamine 1.2 g PO TID
- albuterol HFA PRN
- ferrous sulfate 325 mg PO daily

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; rheumatology 01/16/2024; neurology 3 months. No driving per state law. Return for any seizure.

documents.title: Rheumatology post-hospital letter
documents.author: rheumatology
documents.body:
Outside rheumatology - visit 01/16/2024.
Seen after admission for neuropsychiatric lupus with seizure. No further events. Prednisone now 35 mg on taper. Malar rash nearly resolved. No arthritis. Plan: complete taper to 10 mg; continue hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily; levetiracetam per neurology. CBC and CMP in February through primary care, please forward. Return 3 months.

events.reason: ED record and gynecologic oncology discharge summary received

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Multiple bilateral pulmonary infiltrates. No pleural effusion. No pneumothorax. Heart size normal. Mediastinum normal.

Transabdominal and transvaginal. Uterus enlarged. Heterogeneous, markedly vascular endometrial tissue measuring 2.4 cm. No gestational sac or intrauterine pregnancy. Ovaries normal in size bilaterally. No free fluid.
reports.conclusion: Enlarged uterus with 2.4 cm heterogeneous vascular endometrial tissue; no pregnancy. In this setting consistent with gestational trophoblastic neoplasia.

reports.text: CT chest with IV contrast. Six pulmonary nodules in both lungs, the largest 1.4 cm in the right lower lobe. No pulmonary embolism. No mediastinal or hilar adenopathy. No pleural effusion. Visualized upper abdomen unremarkable.
reports.conclusion: Six bilateral pulmonary nodules, largest 1.4 cm, consistent with metastases in the clinical setting.

reports.study: MRI brain without and with contrast
reports.text: Staging. No enhancing lesion. No hemorrhage. No mass effect. No vascular malformation. Normal ventricles.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 06/08/2024, 19:45.

CC: shortness of breath, vaginal bleeding.
HPI: 34-year-old woman with Crohn's, SLE (neuropsychiatric lupus with seizure 12/2023) and HHT, recent rectovaginal fistula with seton. Two weeks of shortness of breath and irregular vaginal bleeding, heavier than her periods. Miscarriage at 10 weeks gestation followed by D&C three months ago.
Meds: mesalamine, hydroxychloroquine, prednisone 10 mg, albuterol PRN, ferrous sulfate. NKDA.

Vitals: BP 130/85, HR 102, RR 22, SpO2 94% on room air, afebrile.
Exam: mildly tachypneic. Diffuse rales both lungs. Abdomen soft; uterus palpably enlarged.

Labs: Hgb 11.2, WBC 7.8, platelets 250. Serum beta-hCG 225,000 mIU/mL.
CXR: multiple bilateral pulmonary infiltrates.

Assessment: markedly elevated hCG three months after a pregnancy loss with an enlarged uterus and lung infiltrates - gestational trophoblastic neoplasia with pulmonary metastases until proven otherwise. Gynecologic oncology consulted; admitted.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology discharge summary
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Regional hospital - Gynecologic Oncology. Admitted 06/08/2024, discharged 06/13/2024.

Diagnosis: choriocarcinoma (post-abortal gestational trophoblastic neoplasia) metastatic to lung. FIGO stage III. WHO/FIGO prognostic score 7 (high risk): antecedent abortion, hCG >100,000, more than four lung metastases.

Workup: pelvic ultrasound - enlarged uterus with 2.4 cm heterogeneous vascular endometrial tissue, no pregnancy. CT chest - six bilateral nodules, largest 1.4 cm. MRI brain - no metastasis. Tissue biopsy not pursued (hemorrhage risk; diagnosis on clinical and hCG criteria).

Treatment: EMA/CO (etoposide, methotrexate, actinomycin D / cyclophosphamide, vincristine) cycle 1 started 06/12/2024 with folinic acid rescue; tolerated. Oxygen weaned to room air by 06/11.

Discharge medications: home medications unchanged (mesalamine, hydroxychloroquine, prednisone 10 mg, levetiracetam 500 mg BID, albuterol, ferrous sulfate).

Follow-up: cancer center infusion every 2 weeks; weekly hCG. Avoid pregnancy; reliable contraception. Primary care: routine.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology progress letter
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Cancer center - gynecologic oncology. Visit 07/16/2024.
Cycle 3 of EMA/CO given. hCG falling appropriately: 225,000 at presentation, 8,420 on 07/09. Breathing normal. Fatigue as expected; no neutropenic fever. Continue EMA/CO every 2 weeks with weekly hCG; consolidation for three cycles after the first normal value.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology progress letter
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body: Cancer center - gynecologic oncology. hCG 212 on 08/06 and 4 on 09/03 (normal <5). First normal value reached. Plan three consolidation cycles of EMA/CO, last expected mid-October, then monthly hCG surveillance for 12 months. Tolerating treatment.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology end-of-treatment letter
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Cancer center - gynecologic oncology. Visit 10/22/2024.
Completed EMA/CO, final consolidation cycle 10/15/2024. hCG normal since 09/03. Complete remission.
Surveillance: monthly hCG for 12 months. Pregnancy should be avoided for 12 months after completion of chemotherapy so that hCG can be followed; contraception reviewed with patient and partner. Return to work when energy allows. We will send hCG results periodically.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology surveillance letter
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Cancer center - gynecologic oncology. Surveillance update.
Monthly hCG since completing EMA/CO: <2 mIU/mL on 11/19, 12/17, 1/14, 2/11 and 3/11. Remains in remission. Continue monthly hCG through October 2025, then every 3 months. Continue contraception until then.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology letter
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Cancer center - gynecologic oncology.
Unplanned pregnancy about 7 months after completing EMA/CO for choriocarcinoma. hCG 1,840 on 4/29. Ultrasound 5/20: single intrauterine gestation, about 7 weeks, cardiac activity present. hCG surveillance suspended during pregnancy. Plan: hCG 6 weeks after delivery and placental pathology at delivery; patient informed. Discussed with her OB team.

documents.title: Hydroxychloroquine retinal screening
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body: Outside ophthalmology - exam 07/22/2025. Hydroxychloroquine, about 6 years. Pregnant, second trimester. Acuity 20/20 OU, dilated exam normal, 10-2 fields full, OCT normal. No toxicity. Annual screening.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 12/28/2025, 18:10.

CC: fever, incision pain.
HPI: 36-year-old woman with Crohn's disease and SLE, postoperative day 3 after emergency cesarean delivery for fetal distress. Pain and redness around the incision since this morning; temperature 38.5 C at home. Breastfeeding.
Meds: mesalamine 1.2 g TID, hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily, prednisone 10 mg daily, albuterol PRN, ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily. NKDA.

Vitals: T 38.5 C; remaining vital signs within normal limits. BMI 34.
Exam: Low transverse cesarean incision with surrounding erythema and induration and a small amount of purulent drainage; no foul odor. No fluctuance. No crepitus. Abdomen otherwise soft. Fundus firm, appropriately tender. Breasts without erythema.

Labs: WBC 14.0, CRP 86 mg/L.
Wound culture sent.

Assessment: superficial incisional surgical site infection (cellulitis) after cesarean.
Plan: cephalexin 500 mg PO four times daily for 7 days. Wound care instructions. Follow-up with OB tomorrow as scheduled. Return for spreading redness, worsening pain or persistent fever.

documents.title: Obstetrics postpartum visit, day 4
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside OB/MFM group. Date of service 12/29/2025.

Postpartum day 4 after emergency cesarean. Seen in ED yesterday for incisional cellulitis, on cephalexin; afebrile today.
Complaint: both breasts painful and swollen. Trying to breastfeed; baby not latching well and she worries the baby isn't getting enough. No fever today, no nipple discharge, no red streaking.
Vitals within normal limits.
Exam: breasts symmetrically enlarged, firm, tender. No skin color change. Nipples intact without cracks or fissures. No palpable axillary nodes. Incision: erythema receding, no drainage.
Assessment: postpartum breast engorgement. Mild incisional cellulitis improving.
Plan: feed or express every 2-3 hours, warm compress before and cold after feeds, gentle hand expression to soften before latch, same-day lactation consultant visit. Finish cephalexin. Postpartum visit at 4 weeks.

documents.title: Obstetrics postpartum visit, 4 weeks
documents.author: obstetrics
documents.body:
Outside OB/MFM group. Date of service 01/22/2026.

Routine 4-week postpartum visit; infant along, well and gaining weight. Exclusively breastfeeding. Two days of painful blisters on the right breast. No fever, chills or flu-like illness. No recent vaccines, no sick contacts. Engorgement resolved.
Vitals within normal limits.
Exam: grouped vesicles on an erythematous base confined to the right areola. No similar lesions elsewhere. Incision healed.
Labs: HIV antibody negative. CBC within normal limits. RPR nonreactive.
Assessment: herpes simplex infection of the right areola.
Plan: valacyclovir 1 g twice daily for 7 days. Breastfeed from the left; pump and discard from the right until all lesions are crusted. Hand hygiene. Return as needed.

Medications listed: mesalamine, hydroxychloroquine, prednisone 10 mg, albuterol, ferrous sulfate. NKDA.

reports.text: Noncontrast CT head. Hemorrhagic lesion in the left parietal lobe with surrounding vasogenic edema. No midline shift. No hydrocephalus. No other intracranial hemorrhage. Calvarium intact.
CT angiogram of the chest. No pulmonary embolism. Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules. No pleural or pericardial effusion. Heart size normal. No mediastinal adenopathy.
reports.conclusion: Multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules. No pulmonary embolism.

reports.study: MRI brain without and with contrast
reports.text: Single 2.1 cm enhancing hemorrhagic lesion in the left parietal lobe with surrounding edema and mild local mass effect. No additional lesions. No vascular malformation. Ventricles normal.
reports.conclusion: Solitary hemorrhagic left parietal metastasis, 2.1 cm.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 07/01/2026, 13:30. Stroke alert.

HPI: 36-year-old woman, about six months after delivery, with SLE, Crohn's disease, HHT and choriocarcinoma treated in 2024. Abrupt right-sided weakness and difficulty speaking this afternoon. In recent weeks she had spells of lightheadedness and an intermittent dull chest discomfort she had not mentioned to anyone. No follow-up care since her postpartum visit. No hypertension, diabetes or prior stroke. No drug use, recent travel or trauma.
Meds: mesalamine, hydroxychloroquine, prednisone 10 mg, albuterol PRN, ferrous sulfate. NKDA.

Vitals: T 37.1 C (98.8 F), BP 118/76, HR 92.
Exam: awake and alert. Expressive aphasia. Right facial droop. Right arm and leg weakness. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender.

Labs: Hgb 10.8, WBC 7.9, platelets 242. Serum beta-hCG 75,300 mIU/mL.
CT head: hemorrhagic left parietal lesion. CTA chest: multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules, no PE.
Not a thrombolysis candidate (hemorrhage).

Assessment: hemorrhagic brain lesion with lung nodules and high hCG after a term pregnancy, in a patient with prior choriocarcinoma - metastatic gestational trophoblastic neoplasia. Admitted; gyn onc and neurosurgery consulted.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Regional hospital - Gynecologic Oncology. Admitted 07/01/2026, discharged 07/11/2026.

Diagnosis: choriocarcinoma metastatic to brain and lungs, presenting six months after a term cesarean delivery; prior post-abortal choriocarcinoma 2024 treated to remission. FIGO stage IV, prognostic score 15 (ultra-high risk).

Course: MRI brain 7/2: single 2.1 cm hemorrhagic enhancing left parietal metastasis with edema, no other lesions. Dexamethasone 4 mg IV every 6 hours. Levetiracetam continued; no seizures. Neurosurgery: no operation at present. Low-dose etoposide-cisplatin induction started 07/03 to lower the risk of tumor bleeding; EP/EMA with high-dose methotrexate for CNS disease to begin 07/17 at the cancer center. Breastfeeding stopped. PT, OT and speech therapy daily: right arm and leg strength improving, speech improving.

Discharge exam: mild expressive word-finding difficulty, right grip 4/5, right leg 4+/5, walking without device.

Discharge medications: dexamethasone 2 mg PO BID with taper per oncology; levetiracetam 500 mg BID; hydroxychloroquine 200 mg daily; prednisone 10 mg daily; mesalamine 1.2 g TID; ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily; albuterol PRN.

Follow-up: cancer center 07/17 to begin EP/EMA; hCG every 2 weeks with cycles; outpatient PT, OT and speech therapy referrals placed; PCP within 1 week. No driving.

documents.title: Gynecologic oncology progress letter
documents.author: gynecologic oncology
documents.body:
Cancer center - gynecologic oncology. Visit 08/11/2026.
Choriocarcinoma, FIGO IV:15, on EP/EMA with high-dose methotrexate since 07/17 after etoposide-cisplatin induction. hCG 75,300 (7/1), 41,200 (7/14), 6,880 (7/28), 1,124 (8/11) - responding. No new neurological symptoms; speech and right-sided strength improving with therapy. Dexamethasone taper completed 08/07. Continue EP/EMA, hCG with each cycle. Radiation oncology opinion on the brain lesion to be revisited once hCG is normal.
